part1.title: Part 1 – Look and read
part1.instruction: Choose the correct words and write them on the lines. There is one example.

example.text: This person works outside on a large piece of land, growing crops and looking after animals like cows and sheep.

questions.text: You go to this big building to buy all kinds of food, drinks and things you need for your house, and you pay at a till.
This warm piece of outdoor clothing has buttons or a zip down the front and has long sleeves. You wear it when it is cold outside.
This is a wild animal from Australia. It has very powerful back legs and can jump very high. The mother carries her baby in a pouch.
You go to this dark building to sit in comfortable seats and watch the newest films on a very large screen with other people.
This doctor's job is to look at your teeth, clean them carefully, and fix any problems to keep them healthy and strong.

part2.title: Part 2 – Short Dialogues
part2.instruction: Read the dialogues and choose the best answer (A, B or C). There is one example.

example.speaker: Sally
example.question: Did you enjoy your birthday party yesterday, Fred?
options: A) Yes, it was absolutely fantastic!
B) I am nine years old today.
C) The party starts at four o'clock.

questions.speaker: Sally
questions.question: How many friends came to your birthday party in the end?
options: A) About eight or nine friends came.
B) Yes, they all came together.
C) They were very happy to be there.

questions.speaker: Sally
questions.question: What kind of birthday cake did your mum make for you?
options: A) She made a huge chocolate cake!
B) Yes, my mum can cook very well.
C) The cake is on the kitchen table.

questions.speaker: Sally
questions.question: Did you get lots of nice presents to unwrap?
options: A) Yes! I got a brand new bicycle!
B) No, it is not mine at all.
C) I always like receiving presents.

questions.speaker: Sally
questions.question: Who gave you the cool red safety helmet for your bike?
options: A) My grandparents bought it for me.
B) He is my favourite uncle.
C) Yes, it is a very nice red colour.

questions.speaker: Sally
questions.question: Can I come and ride your new bike with you this afternoon?
options: A) Yes, let's go after we finish our homework!
B) No, the bike was yellow before.
C) I already rode my bike this morning.

questions.speaker: Sally
questions.question: Great! I'll see you at three o'clock at the park then!
options: A) Perfect! Bye! See you there later!
B) Yes, I do like going to the park.
C) Thank you so very much for coming.

part3.title: Part 3 – Complete the Story
part3.instruction: Read the story. Choose a word from the box. Write the correct word next to numbers 1–5. There is one example.
part3.storyText: Yesterday morning, Charlie decided he wanted to make surprise pancakes for his mum's [example: birthday]. He crept into the (1) ________ very quietly and slowly while his mum was still sleeping. He found some eggs, a bottle of milk, and a bag of white (2) ________ in the kitchen cupboard. He followed the (3) ________ from a cookery book step by step, but when he started mixing everything together in a large bowl, he accidentally knocked the spoon off the counter and it made a huge (4) ________ all over the floor! Charlie felt worried and upset, so he started (5) ________ the table and mopping the floor as fast as he could with a cloth. Just then, his mum walked in and looked completely (6) ________! 'Happy Birthday, Mum!' Charlie said proudly. They laughed together and finished making the most (7) ________ pancakes with maple syrup!

titleQuestion.question: Now choose the best name for the story. Tick one box.
options: A surprise breakfast for Mum
Charlie's favourite cookery book
A trip to the supermarket

part4.title: Part 4 – Factual Text
part4.instruction: Read the text. Choose the right words and write them on the lines.
paragraphs: Elephants are the largest land animals in (1) ________ world. There are two main types: the African elephant and the Asian elephant, and African elephants are the bigger of the two.
An elephant has a very long nose which is (2) ________ a trunk. Elephants use their trunks for many things, such as picking up food and leaves, drinking water, and even washing their bodies.
They eat only plants, grass, leaves and fruit every day, but they never (3) ________ meat at all. A large adult elephant needs to eat about 150 kilograms of food every single day to stay healthy!

Elephants are very intelligent and have excellent memories. They live in groups (4) ________ by an older female elephant called the matriarch, who leads the whole family and helps them find water and food.
Baby elephants are called calves. They stay very close (5) ________ their mothers for many years to learn how to find food, how to use their trunk, and how to survive safely in the wild.

part5.title: Part 5 – Complete Sentences about the Story
part5.instruction: Look at the pictures and read the story. Write 1, 2 or 3 words to complete the sentences about the story. You can use words from the story.
part5.storyTitle: 🦒 Ben's trip to the city zoo

storyPassages.text: Last Tuesday, Ben and the rest of his class took a long journey on a big blue school bus to visit the city zoo with their teacher, Miss Green. Ben was incredibly excited because he had always wanted to see the tall and graceful giraffes up close. He brought his camera with him in his bag so he could take lots of photographs to show his family at home.

First, Miss Green took the class to visit the monkey house, which was one of the noisiest places in the whole zoo. A cheeky little brown monkey suddenly jumped right down from a branch above and tried to grab Ben's yellow banana from inside his bag! Everyone burst out laughing loudly, and even the monkeys seemed to be enjoying the joke.

Next, Miss Green gathered everyone together and took a group photograph of the whole class standing in front of the lion enclosure. The lions were lying lazily in the afternoon sun. At the end of the long and wonderful afternoon, Ben visited the zoo gift shop and used his pocket money to buy a small toy giraffe to take home as a souvenir. He said it was the best school trip he had ever been on.
